Geez, for some reason I thought they had at least some mods. Alright well, I have a lot of hours on Ark, something close to 2500 if I remember correctly. I spent 700 hours of that on Official servers, and the rest on a variety of private servers that were all modded. I'm not sure if you're familiar with what some of the mods for Ark do, but here are a few that tend to get used on pretty much every server I've played on.

Stack mods. Honestly, this is the one I'm amazed that they didn't have an "official" mod or something for the consoles. Basically it's a mod that allows servers to change how much items weigh, and how many of each item can be in one stack. Most private servers use this, and it is such a quality of life change.

There is a mod called "S+" which means Structure Plus, and it adds a new engram for every single Structure in the game. You can craft S+ Stone Foundations for instance. Everything is pretty much the same as vanilla, but like for stone walls, the wooden "inner" side of the wall is gone. So there's a few aesthetic changes but it's mostly about the ability to pick up structures you've placed. Which for me is a damned game changer. It also adds in walls that are 4, 8, and 12 normal walls tall. I can't tell you how many times I've placed something and it didn't snap to the existing structure properly and I had to destroy the damn thing, it's especialllllly useful for placing gates.

ORP for PVP servers is Offline Raid Protection, it gives the server the option to set a multiplier for your Dinosaurs and Structures HP while your tribe is offline. Most commonly I see it set at 4x, so all your structures have four times the health when you're offline. Some servers have it set to 10x, which is what I prefer. It doesn't make offline raiding impossible, but it seriously encourages people to do online raiding. Brings a bit of life back into PVP, because in my opinion, with over two thousand hours on Ark and Rust, raiding is just too fucking easy on Ark. It's so cut throat for solo players, on active servers most of them get wiped out overnight unless there's ORP, then it makes people think twice about where they want to waste their C4.

There are mods that alter the Beacon drops as well, or whatever you want to call them. Allows the server admin to set what items can drop in what colored beacons, etc etc. I feel the beacons in vanilla were practically useless, and having relevant stuff drop gives players a reason to explore the map more. Little things like that breath more life into the game, makes the map you're on feel more alive.

Those are all fairly mild though, there's one mod called Annunaki that I remember, it had tons of reskinned dinosaurs. They had elemental versions of existing dinosaurs, like Fire, Ice, Stone, and Poison. Poison Elemental Dinosaurs caused torpor on hit, so getting a decent Poison Argent was great. All the elemental dinosaurs had custom effects, like the poison Argents had a green glow surrounding them, and were recolored to be mostly black and green. Fire had a red glow, reskinned red/black etc. It was fairly well done aesthetically. It also had "Primal Alphas" which were an upgraded and even nastier version of Alpha dinosaurs, plus they made regular Alpha dinosaurs tameable, and included Alpha versions of almost every single Dinosaur where in Vanilla I'm pretty sure there's just a handful of Alphas types. They're still pretty rare though. There were also a few other "tiers" of Dinosaur in it, as well as a couple uh, I can't remember the term they used, but for lack of better words "super dinos", one being a pretty awesome looking Dragon with a custom skin. PVP servers with that mod were a bit crazy though. They usually had other mods as well, like new tiers of autoturrets and stuff like that in order to balance the more powerful dinosaurs.

These mods fundamentally change the game for me, I was done after those first seven hundred hours. The Official servers were a damned nightmare. I can guarantee I wouldn't have continued playing past that point if mods didn't exist. The thing is, I have experiences like this with dozens of games. Mods are such a major aspect of gaming for me.
